stops.note: meaning "a camp" or "royal court", used by nomadic peoples
the Golden Horde ruled Russia from the 1240s; Mongol 'ordu', camp, gave the name
borrowed in the 1550s for Asian tent-dwelling nomads; the initial 'h' seems to have been added in Polish
stops.meaning: a large, often disorganized group of people

current_meaning: a large, often disorganized group or crowd of people
